title: Tensor compatibility of strict henselizations for a finite map
statement:
Let $A\to B$ be a finite ring map and $A\to C$ any ring map [def-weil-finite-integral-morphism]. Let $\Omega$ be an algebraically closed field with a geometric point of $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_A C)$ [def-weil-geometric-point, def-pc-fibre-product], and let $p$, $q$, $r$ and $m$ be the induced primes of $A$, $B$, $C$ and $B\otimes_A C$. Form the strict henselizations $A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $C_r^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $(B\otimes_A C)_m^{\mathrm{sh}}$ using the pointed etale-neighbourhood construction and the embeddings into $\Omega$ [def-weil-pbc-strict-henselization-limit]. The canonical map induced by the four structure maps is an isomorphism
$$B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}\otimes_{A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}}C_r^{\mathrm{sh}}\cong(B\otimes_AC)_m^{\mathrm{sh}}.$$
It is compatible with the maps to $\operatorname{Spec}B$, $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $\operatorname{Spec}(B\otimes_AC)$, and with the chosen geometric point.

proof.text: Put $D=B\otimes_A C$, $H_A=A_p^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $H_B=B_q^{\mathrm{sh}}$, $H_C=C_r^{\mathrm{sh}}$ and $H_D=D_m^{\mathrm{sh}}$. Apply strict-henselization functoriality to the four projections of affine spectra at the given geometric points. Its clauses (1)-(3) give local rings, their canonical evaluations $\epsilon_X:H_X\to\Omega$ with maximal-ideal kernels, and local maps between them inducing the inclusions of the separable residue closures inside the same $\Omega$. The two composites $H_A\to H_D$ agree: they have the same structural map and residue inclusion, so uniqueness in clause (3) applies. The tensor universal property therefore gives the specified map $c:E=H_B\otimes_{H_A}H_C\to H_D$, $b\otimes z\mapsto h_{BD}(b)h_{CD}(z)$. Its evaluation is $\epsilon_E(b\otimes z)=\epsilon_B(b)\epsilon_C(z)$, and $\epsilon_Dc=\epsilon_E$.

If $b_1,\ldots,b_n$ generate $B$ as an $A$-module, then $b_i\otimes1$ generate $D$ as a $C$-module: expand the first factor of each pure tensor and absorb its $A$-coefficients in the second factor. Thus $C\to D$ is finite as well. The finite-ring-map lemma makes $A\to B$ finite type and quasi-finite at $q$, and $C\to D$ finite type and quasi-finite at $m$. Apply the quasi-finite strict-henselization lemma to both maps, with the compatible residue embeddings into $\Omega$. It gives $H_B$ finite local over $H_A$, with finite purely inseparable residue extension, and canonical descriptions
$$H_B=(H_A\otimes_{A_p}B_q)_Q,\qquad H_D=(H_C\otimes_{C_r}D_m)_{P_0},$$
where $Q,P_0$ are the kernels of the respective evaluations into $\Omega$. Both descriptions commute with the displayed structural ring maps.

Write $V=B\otimes_A H_A$ and $R=B\otimes_A H_C$, and put $\widetilde Q=\ker(V\to\Omega)$ and $P=\ker(R\to\Omega)$. The formulas in Step 2 yield $H_B=V_{\widetilde Q}$ and $H_D=R_P$: passing from $B$ to $B_q$ first only inverts elements whose evaluations are nonzero, and the final prime localization already inverts them; the same argument applies to $D\to D_m$ and $C\to C_r$. If $U=V\setminus\widetilde Q$ and $\overline U$ is its image in $R$, the tensor relations identify
$$E=V_{\widetilde Q}\otimes_{H_A}H_C=\overline U^{-1}R.$$
Explicitly $(v/u)\otimes z$ maps to $(v\otimes z)/\overline u$ after $V\otimes_{H_A}H_C=R$; conversely the maps $R\to E$ and $\overline u\mapsto u\otimes1$ send every denominator to a unit and give the inverse fraction map. Both composites fix pure tensors and inverses, hence all elements. Since $\overline U\cap P=\varnothing$, the map $c$ becomes precisely the localization map $\overline U^{-1}R\to R_P$. These are canonical identifications preserving evaluation.

proof.text: By Step 2, $H_A\to H_B$ is finite local with purely inseparable residue extension, while $H_A\to H_C$ is local by Step 1. The finite-algebra integrality lemma makes $H_B$ integral over $H_A$. Apply the integral-local tensor lemma with $(R,S,T)=(H_A,H_B,H_C)$ and its first residue-field alternative to conclude that $E$ is local. Also $E$ is finite over $H_C$: if $e_1,\ldots,e_a$ generate $H_B$ over $H_A$, the tensors $e_i\otimes1$ generate $E$ over $H_C$, by the same expansion as Step 2. Applying finite-algebra integrality again makes $E$ integral over $H_C$. No Noetherian hypothesis on any ring is used.

proof.text: The prime $N=\ker(\epsilon_E:E\to\Omega)$ contracts in $H_C$ to $\ker\epsilon_C=\mathfrak m_{H_C}$ by Step 1. Step 4 says $E$ is integral over $H_C$, so the integral-prime-over-maximal lemma shows $N$ is maximal. Since $E$ is local, $N=\mathfrak m_E$. Under Step 3 its contraction to $R$ is exactly $P$. Every $a\in R\setminus P$ consequently has image outside $\mathfrak m_E$, hence a unit in $E$. There is therefore a map $d:R_P\to E$ sending $a/s$ to the image of $a$ times the inverse of the image of $s$. The composites $cd$ and $dc$ fix every element of $R$ and every inverted denominator; the universal property of each fraction ring makes them identities. This proves that the specified $c$, rather than an unrelated ring isomorphism, is invertible. It supplies the small detail omitted in Stacks 0GIP.

proof.text: The canonical map $c$ was defined using the two functorial strict-henselization maps, and the localization identifications fixed the maps from $B$, $C$ and $D=B\otimes_A C$. Thus its spectrum commutes with the structural maps to $\operatorname{Spec}B$, $\operatorname{Spec}C$ and $\operatorname{Spec}D$. The equality $\epsilon_Dc=\epsilon_E$ of Step 1 gives preservation of the chosen geometric point. Composing these equalities with the inverse of $c$ gives the same compatibility for the inverse. This proves every compatibility in the statement.

reviewed.note: mechanical checks by tools/merge_delivery.py; mathematics reviewed in full by NT-cc-Q02-5781c53d2 (reviewer sub-agent of L); spot-checked: I read the item, its 6 steps and the new node in full, and checked them against Stacks algebra.tex 0GIP (statement and proof of case (1)), 05WR and 092Y. The item statement is unchanged and is the finite case of 0GIP with the canonical tensor base-change map. Steps: (1) the uniqueness in functoriality clause (3) makes the two maps H_A->H_D agree, which gives c with eps_D c = eps_E. (2) C->D is finite by an explicit generator argument, and the quasi-finite-ring node (05WR) gives the two localization models plus finite local H_A->H_B with purely inseparable residue extension. (3) The localization identities H_B=V_Q~, H_D=R_P and E=U^-1 R, with U disjoint from P, are verified and acceptable as elementary. (4) The 092Y node applied to (H_A,H_B,H_C) makes E local, and E is integral over H_C. (5) ker eps_E is maximal (integral over the maximal ideal of H_C), hence equals m_E, so R\P becomes units and E=R_P; this fills 0GIP's 'small detail omitted' correctly. (6) Spec and geometric-point compatibilities hold. proof_deps equals the union of uses, and no SGA source is cited. The new node lem-trf-integral-local-tensor-purely-inseparable is 092Y with the factors swapped, with exactly its hypotheses (local maps, one map integral, either residue extension purely inseparable). I tested it on R=S; on R=IR, S=T=C, where the hypothesis fails and the tensor product C x C is not local; and on F_p(t^{1/p}) over F_p(t), where the tensor product S[eps]/eps^p is local. It is not a duplicate: grep finds no other node citing 092Y or 0GIP that states it. Its Mathlib searches are logged with no match. The slopmaster2 declaration Algebra.isLocalRing_tensorProduct_of_isPurelyInseparable_residueField (IntegralLocal.lean:510-522, no sorry in the file) states the node exactly and can be attached. No fixes were needed. Full details are in review.md.
